# UX and customer research

<!-- Generated by scripts/package/render_roles.py. Edit the YAML source, not this file. -->

**Department id:** `ux-research`  
**Mission:** Learn how real people behave, decide and struggle, and make the evidence usable by product and design.

## Startup stage

Founders run interviews themselves with a script and a consent note; synthesis is shared with design. Never let the absence of a researcher turn into invented personas.

## Agents operating in this department

`customer-researcher`, `ux-auditor`

## Roles

### UX researcher

Role id: `ux-researcher`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Plan, run and synthesise studies that answer design and product questions. |
| Scope of responsibility | Interviews, surveys, usability tests, diary studies, journey mapping. |
| Core activities | Write research plan and screener; Run non-leading sessions; Synthesise findings with severity; Map journeys |
| Inputs | Research questions; Prototypes; Recruiting access |
| Outputs and deliverables | Research plan; Findings report; Personas (evidence-based or labelled hypothesis); Journey maps |
| Decisions it can make | Method and sample |
| Decisions requiring approval | Participant recruitment; consent; incentives; personal data |
| Collaborating roles | product; design; research |
| Reporting relationship | design-lead |
| KPIs | Findings adopted into design; Issues found before build |
| Quality expectations | No fabricated quotes or counts; interpretation separated from observation |
| Tools and resources | Interview guide template; Findings template |
| Common failure modes | Leading questions; Friends as participants; Simulated personas presented as research |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Recruitment and data handling |

### Usability test facilitator and analyst

Role id: `usability-tester`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Measure whether people can complete critical tasks and why not. |
| Scope of responsibility | Moderated and unmoderated usability tests, task success, severity ranking. |
| Core activities | Define tasks and success criteria; Facilitate sessions; Rank issues by severity and frequency; Retest |
| Inputs | Prototype or product; Task list |
| Outputs and deliverables | Usability report; Severity-ranked issues; Retest results |
| Decisions it can make | Task design |
| Decisions requiring approval | Participants and consent |
| Collaborating roles | design; qa |
| Reporting relationship | design-lead |
| KPIs | Task success rate; Issues fixed and retested |
| Quality expectations | Success rates only from real sessions |
| Tools and resources | Usability test template |
| Common failure modes | Invented success rates; No retest |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Participants |

### Customer research analyst

Role id: `customer-research-analyst`

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| Mission | Understand jobs, triggers, workarounds and spending across segments. |
| Scope of responsibility | Jobs-to-be-done, segmentation by behaviour, willingness-to-pay signals. |
| Core activities | Behavioural interviews; Segment by need and context; Capture spending and alternatives |
| Inputs | Segment hypotheses; Interview access |
| Outputs and deliverables | Customer findings; Segment definitions; JTBD statements |
| Decisions it can make | Segmentation proposal |
| Decisions requiring approval | Participant data |
| Collaborating roles | research; strategy; product |
| Reporting relationship | research-lead |
| KPIs | Segments validated by behaviour; WTP evidence collected |
| Quality expectations | Sample size and bias stated |
| Tools and resources | Interview guide; Evidence ledger |
| Common failure modes | Hypothetical would-you-use-it questions; Demographic-only segments |
| Appropriate AI autonomy | propose |
| Human approval requirements | Participant data |
